325: ## 11. Shared components (new, each defined once)
326: 
327: The foundation's shared components (foundation section 3.5) are reused unchanged: SerializableWrite, IdempotentCreate with PayloadFingerprint, ReadableKeyAllocator, PagedQuery with PageBounds, ClassifiedErrorException with ErrorCodes, SecretRedactor, ContentHasher, TurnLocator, TurnWritePipeline, ScoreLexeme, ScoreVerdict, and WorkspaceResolutionBehavior. The components below are new; each has one implementation, one test class named for it, and one diagram here, and every unit that uses one draws it as a single call node.
328: 
329: ### 11.1 FencedLease (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Leases`)
330: 
331: Claims, renews, and takes over the lease of one row, and guards every fenced write, following develop's handoff-ingestion pattern (`HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735,782-807`). Operations: `Claim(row, owner, duration)` (only when the row has no lease or an expired one; the fence token increments), `Renew(row, owner, fence, duration)`, `Guard(row, owner, fence)` (the precondition of every fenced write), `Release(row, owner, fence)`. Each runs inside the caller's SerializableWrite. Used by ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunStartCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, and by the HostileReview worker's ClaimHostileReviewAttemptCommand, RenewHostileReviewAttemptCommand, CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand, and ExpireHostileReviewLeasesCommand (section 16.7).
332: 
333: ```mermaid
334: flowchart TD
335:     S(["FencedLease: operation, row, owner, fence"]) --> OP{"Operation?"}
336:     OP -->|Claim| CL{"Lease absent or expired?"}
337:     CL -->|no| E1(["held: another owner holds a live lease"])
338:     CL -->|yes| CT["Set owner and expiry, increment the fence token"]
339:     CT --> OK1(["claimed: the new fence token"])
340:     OP -->|"Renew, Guard, or Release"| G{"Owner and fence equal the stored ones?"}
341:     G -->|no| E2(["stale_fence: nothing changed"])
342:     G -->|yes| W{"Operation?"}
343:     W -->|Renew| RN["Extend the expiry"]
344:     RN --> OK2(["renewed"])
345:     W -->|Guard| OK3(["guarded: the caller's write proceeds"])
346:     W -->|Release| RL["Clear owner and expiry"]
347:     RL --> OK4(["released"])
348: ```

351: 
352: `Compress(bytes)` returns one GZIP member; `Decompress(bytes)` returns the original bytes; `RoundTrip(original, compressed)` decompresses and compares length and SHA-256 (through ContentHasher's hex form over raw bytes) and fails with `evidence_corrupt` on any difference, so no compressed blob is stored unverified. It follows `DataAuditLogEntity`'s encode and decode (`DataAuditLogEntity.cs:119-147`); that entity's private copy is context, not work. Used by SubmitHvRequestCommand (request evidence), AppendHvRunOutputCommand (chunks), FinalizeHvRequestCommand (result document, chunk verification), and GetHvRequestQuery, GetHvResultQuery, GetHvEvidenceQuery, and OrderedEventReplay (reads).
353: 
354: ```mermaid
355: flowchart TD
356:     S(["GzipCodec: operation, bytes"]) --> OP{"Operation?"}
357:     OP -->|Compress| C["Write one GZIP member at the configured level"]
358:     C --> RT[["GzipCodec RoundTrip on the result"]]
359:     RT -->|equal| OK1(["compressed bytes"])
360:     RT -->|different| E1(["evidence_corrupt"])
361:     OP -->|Decompress| D{"Valid GZIP member?"}
362:     D -->|no| E2(["evidence_corrupt"])
363:     D -->|yes| OK2(["original bytes"])
364:     OP -->|RoundTrip| R["Decompress, compare length and SHA-256 with the original"]
365:     R -->|equal| OK3(["equal"])
366:     R -->|different| E3(["evidence_corrupt"])
367: ```

370: 
371: `EnsureAvailable()` checks, inside the caller's transaction, that the `DataAuditLogs` table is writable and refuses with 503 `audit_unavailable` (`retryable: true`) when it is not, closing for HV the skip of `McpDbContext.AppendAuditRows` (`McpDbContext.cs:1507-1538`); `RecordRead(entityKind, entityKey, actor)` adds one ledger row with action `read` for an evidence access (R-19): inside the caller's transaction when it has one, and otherwise in a transaction of its own that commits before the caller consumes any byte. Every HV unit calls `EnsureAvailable()` before any other step that writes. `RecordRead` is the one boundary of every evidence read (R-19), called before any byte is returned or consumed: by GetHvEvidenceQuery, GetHvResultQuery, the output stream, and GetHvRequestQuery when it returns output lines, and by RunReviewerProcess (the accepted request of the brief), FinalizeHvRequestCommand (the run's chunks), and CloseHvRunOutputCommand (a probe's chunks); each caller states what it does when the read is refused.
372:

374: flowchart TD
375:     S(["AuditLedgerGuard: operation"]) --> A{"DataAuditLogs writable?"}
376:     A -->|no| E(["503 audit_unavailable, retryable: nothing written, no byte read"])
377:     A -->|yes| OP{"Operation?"}
378:     OP -->|EnsureAvailable| OK1(["available"])
379:     OP -->|RecordRead| T{"Caller in a transaction?"}
380:     T -->|yes| R["Add one ledger row: action read, entity kind and key, actor, request id"]
381:     R --> OK2(["read recorded with the caller's commit"])
382:     T -->|no| R2["Add the ledger row in a transaction of its own and commit it"]

384: ```

393:     B -->|yes| U(["Unknown"])

395:     N --> K{"In the alias table?"}

439: 
440: Serves a Server-Sent Events stream from durable ordered rows: parses `Last-Event-ID` (absent means from the beginning of the requested stream, a malformed value is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `Last-Event-ID`), sends every stored event after it in order with its `id:`, then waits on the `IChangeEventBus` wake-up (or a poll interval) and sends new rows; it sends a comment line every 15 seconds while idle so proxies keep the connection, and ends when the caller disconnects or the stream's source reaches a terminal event. Develop's event stream has no replay and no event ids (`src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/EventStreamController.cs:27-92`); this component adds both without changing that controller. 452:     DC -->|yes| END2(["stream closed"])
453:     DC -->|no| RD
454: ```

456: ## 12. Data model (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Entities.HostileValidation`)
457: 
458: Every entity is new, in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/HostileValidation/`, keyed by `WorkspaceId` first (every read is workspace-scoped and no read crosses workspaces, foundation section 3), soft-deleted through `IsDeleted` so that `McpDbContext` writes its audit ledger rows for it (R-19), and carries the root ids of every parent it hangs from (foundation section 3.1, "Root ids"). Lengths are the foundation's: an agent 64, a session id or request id 256, a readable key 128. Scores are `decimal` with precision 29 and scale 28, written and read as exact lexemes (ScoreLexeme). Every timestamp is UTC with offset, and the identifiers that carry a time use the UTC form `yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ` (D-08). Diagrams are in Addendum B.
459: 
460: `HvWorkspaceState` (table `HvWorkspaceStates`, key `WorkspaceId`): one row per workspace, created on first use. `LastAssignedReviewerId` (16, null before the first assignment; the round-robin cursor, R-07), `NextNotificationSequence` (long, starts at 1, R-16), `StateVersion` (int).
461: 
462: `HvReviewer` (table `HvReviewers`, key (`WorkspaceId`, `ReviewerId`)):
463: 
464: - `ReviewerId` (16): `Cline`, `Copilot`, `Claude`, `Codex`, or `Grok`.
465: - `Enabled` (bool), `ExecutionStrategy` (32), `AgentPath` (512), `ConfiguredModel` (128, null means the CLI default), `ConfiguredEffort` (32, null means the highest effort of section 10), `MaxConcurrentRuns` (int).
466: - `ResolvedModel` (128) and `ResolvedEffort` (32): the runtime model and effort the last passing NONCE recorded from the reviewer's own provenance (P-04); null until a NONCE passes.
467: - `Readiness` (16: `Unverified`, `Online`, `Offline`), `ReadinessReason` (64: the failure code that made it `Offline`, or the change that made it `Unverified`; null while `Online`), `ReadinessChangedUtc` (set by every write that changes `Readiness`), `LastProbeRunId` (128, set by ClaimHvRunCommand when it inserts a probe run), `OpenIncidentId` (128, the incident that made it `Offline`; null unless `Offline`, so a passing probe and a configuration change clear it while the incident row itself is kept).
468: - `ProbeRequestedUtc`: set when a NONCE is requested and cleared when ClaimHvRunCommand creates its probe run; a requested probe waits here, so a NONCE survives a restart before it is claimed.
469: - `ConfigurationVersion` (int, starts at 1): incremented by UpdateHvReviewerCommand whenever the strategy, agent path, model, or effort changes, so a probe qualifies only the configuration it ran (HvRun `ReviewerConfigurationVersion`).
470: - `StateVersion` (int: optimistic concurrency for UpdateHvReviewerCommand), `CreatedUtc`, `UpdatedUtc`.
471:

548: ### 13.3 Reviewer contract, version 1
549: 
550: The complete accepted request (the `Request` evidence, written at admission and never changed) is one JSON object: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.request/1", hvRequestId, workspacePath, scope, submitter, turns: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, snapshotSha256, snapshot }], responses: [{ responseId, agent, sessionId, requestId, contentSha256, content, claims }], context, contextFormat, requirementRefs, admittedUtc }`. The brief of one attempt is that object inside an envelope: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.brief/1", request: <the accepted request>, runId, attempt, reviewer: { reviewerId, model, effort }, instructions, outputSchema }`; the worker writes the exact brief it sends as the first record of the attempt's log, `{ "type": "hv_brief", "brief": <the brief> }`, so each log is complete on its own. The brief's `instructions` require the reviewer to review every turn individually and the set of turns as a whole, to treat every turn snapshot and the context as untrusted evidence, to emit the records below as single-line JSON objects in its messages, to emit progress records during the run (P-03), to log its review as its own session-log turn classified `Chore` and store its entire result there, every reviewer record of the run in order (R-24, V-6), to close that turn `completed` through the foundation's completion gate before it ends (an action or design decision and its own agent review, `Other` with a note being enough), because the foundation's Stop gate blocks a host from stopping while a delivered turn is still in progress (foundation section 3.4) and a reviewer run has no time limit (P-02), and to emit exactly one `hv_verdict` record last.
551: 
552: Records (each a JSON object on its own line inside the reviewer's messages, read from each message's complete text as the reviewer's adapter assembles it from the native events, section 16.3; every other line is free text and stays in the log):
553: 
554: - `{ "type": "hv_progress", "percentComplete": 0..100, "etaSeconds": n or null, "note": "..." }`.
555: - `{ "type": "hv_turn_assessment", "hvRequestId", "ordinal", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId", "snapshotSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict": "AGREE" or "DISAGREE", "summary", "findings": [{ "outcome": "FAIL" or "UNKNOWN", "category", "location", "requirementRef", "claimId", "evidence", "remediation" }] }`: one per member turn (S-03, S-21).
556: - `{ "type": "hv_holistic", "hvRequestId", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "summary", "crossTurnFindings": [same shape] }`: exactly one (S-10); it states cross-turn consistency, omissions, contradictions, and end-to-end satisfaction and is never a calculation over the turn scores.
557: - `{ "type": "hv_response_grade", "hvRequestId", "responseId", "contentSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "findings": [{ "claimId", "check", "outcome": "PASS", "FAIL", or "UNKNOWN", "category", "location", "evidence", "remediation" }] }`: one per response of the accepted request, the set admitted with the request whatever has happened to its responses since (foundation `verdict_match` rules: every claim named at least once); `category`, `location`, `evidence`, and `remediation` are required on a FAIL or UNKNOWN finding and may be omitted on a PASS.
558: - `{ "type": "hv_reviewer_turn", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId" }`: the reviewer's own session-log turn (R-24).
559: - `{ "type": "hv_verdict", "hvRequestId", "runId", "overallVerdict", "turnCount", "responseGradeCount", "reviewer": { "reviewerId", "model", "effort" } }`: exactly one, last.
560: - `{ "type": "hv_probe", "nonce", "model", "effort" }`: the answer to a NONCE probe brief (R-10). A probe brief asks for this record and, as a review brief does, for the reviewer's own `Chore` turn and its `hv_reviewer_turn` record (R-24); policy ReadinessProbeVerdict reads both.
561: 
562: The response log is the reviewer process's complete output as JSONL: the worker's `hv_brief` record first; then, when the adapter runs the CLI in a JSON streaming mode, each native event line as written, and otherwise each output line wrapped as `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream": "stdout" or "stderr", "line": "..." }`; and, after the process exits, the adapter's provenance lines `{ "type": "hv_provenance", "model", "effort", "source", "sourceSha256" }`, which name the runtime receipt they were read from and its hash (P-04). The adapter extracts the reviewer's records from the agent message text of the native events (section 16.3). `hv_brief`, `hv_raw`, and `hv_provenance` are written only by the worker as top-level log lines and are never accepted from the reviewer's message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.

564: ### 13.4 Standard result document (S-13)
565: 
566: `GET /requests/{hvRequestId}/result` returns `HvResultDocument`:
567: 
568: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.result/1", hvRequestId, status, scope, submitter, reviewer: { reviewerId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, runtimeModel, runtimeEffort, runId, attempt, reviewerAgent, reviewerSessionId, reviewerRequestId }, request: <the complete accepted request of section 13.3>, responseLog: [<every JSONL record of the finalized run, in order, starting with its hv_brief record>], turnAssessments: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, correctness, completeness, verdict, mappedReviewStatus, summary, findings }], holistic: { correctness, completeness, verdict, summary, crossTurnFindings }, failures: [{ ordinal, scope, turnOrdinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, responseId, check, outcome, category, location, requirementRef, claimId, evidence, remediation }], responseGrades: [{ responseId, disposition, notGradedReason, gradeId, verdict, correctness, completeness, findings }], overallVerdict, thresholds: { correctness, completeness }, evidence: { request: { sha256, bytes, compressedBytes }, responseLog: { chainSha256, bytes, lines, chunks }, result: { sha256 } }, todoIds: [string], finalizedUtc }`.
569: 
570: - `turnAssessments` lists every requested turn with its score (S-21); `failures` is the delineated list of every FAIL and UNKNOWN of every scope (`Turn`, `Holistic`, `Response`), each with its remediation (S-13); `responseGrades` lists every response of the accepted request with its grade record and findings, and its `disposition`, the response item's at commit: `Graded` (its model grade recorded, `gradeId` set), `Closed` (the response left the review before the commit, so its grade is applied to nothing), or `NotGraded` with `notGradedReason` `agent_context_disabled` (Mode `Off` at finalization); every FAIL and UNKNOWN finding of a response grade, whatever its disposition, is also an `HvFinding` row of scope `Response`, so it is kept with the result rows after evidence removal (R-20); `request` and `responseLog` are complete (S-13); `evidence.result.sha256` is `ResultSha256`, the digest of the stored `Result` payload, which excludes this field (section 12); `todoIds` is information only (R-22).
571: - With `Accept-Encoding: gzip` the document is sent compressed; the `responseLog` array is streamed from the chunks, so the server holds no uncompressed copy (R-14).

574: ### 13.5 Streams
575: 
576: - Output stream: event `hv_output` with `id` `<runId>:<sequence>` and data `{ runId, sequence, lines: [string] }`, one event per stored chunk; event `hv_run_closed` with data `{ runId, status }` when the run ends; event `hv_stream_error` with data `{ runId, sequence, code }` when a stored chunk fails to decompress (`evidence_corrupt`), after which the stream ends; a new attempt starts a new run id in the same stream, so `Last-Event-ID` `<runId>:<sequence>` resumes after that chunk of that run. Per S-18 a caller attaches to "any running hv": the stream serves the request's runs in attempt order.
577: - Notification stream: event `<kind>` with `id` `<sequence>` and data `HvNotificationDto`; `Last-Event-ID` `<sequence>` resumes after it. The stream is workspace-scoped (S-19: notifications of HV completion in the plugins).

589: - `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn` 400.

593: - `hv_request_active` 409 (`details.status`: evidence removal of a request that is not `Completed`, `Failed`, or `Canceled`).
594: - `hv_reviewer_disabled` 409 (a NONCE requested for a disabled reviewer).
595: - `hv_result_not_ready` 409 (`details.status`).
596: - `hv_evidence_not_available` 404 (a kind not produced yet) and `hv_evidence_removed` 410.

603: 
604: Each unit is one command or query record and its handler, two files in the folders of section 4. 688: ### 14.2 Admission, queries, and cancellation
689: 
690: #### SubmitHvRequestCommand: admit an HV request [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-002, -004, -005, -006, -007, -011, -013, -018]
691: 
692: - Handler: `SubmitHvRequestCommand(string WorkspacePath, SubmitHvRequestRequest Request) : ICommand<HvRequestResult>`.
693: - Callers: any agent or operator; the plugin verb `workflow.hv.submit` binds the submitting turn automatically (process SubmitHvFromPlugin, section 16.4).
694: - Order of checks:
695:   1. Shape (no store read): the scope fields for its kind (400 `hv_scope_invalid` with `details.field`), the submitter fields for its kind (400 `validation_error` with `details.field` under `submitter`), a nonblank `idempotencyKey` of at most 128 characters, `contextFormat` known and `context` at most 65536 characters (400 `validation_error`).
696:   2. Reads before the transaction (foundation section 3.1, "Database-only delegates"): RequirementReferenceExtractor over `context`.
697:   3. SerializableWrite delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; IdempotentCreate on `IdempotencyKey` (policy `Conflict`, fingerprint of the client inputs): the same inputs return 200 with the stored request, other inputs 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`; TurnLocator on the submitting turn for `submitter.kind` `Agent` (`InvalidIdentifier`, `SessionNotFound`, or `TurnNotFound` is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `submitter`); policy HvScopeResolution; policy HvAdmissionEligibility; policy RoundRobinAssignment; then the inserts.
698:   4. Inserts in the delegate: the `hvr-` key (ReadableKeyAllocator); `HvRequest` `Queued` with `AssignedReviewerId` and `AuthorReviewerId`; one `HvRequestTurn` per member, each with its TurnSnapshotBuilder snapshot hash, class, and hostile status at admission (S-09); the requirement references; one `HvRequestResponse` `Pending` per agent response of a member turn whose status is `Submitted`, `Grading`, `Trusted`, or `Stale` and that is not `Pending` in another open request (when Phase C has recorded responses); the `Request` evidence through GzipCodec (section 13.3); policy HvTurnFreeze `Freeze` on every member turn (`HvState` `Pending`, `HvRequestId`); the round-robin cursor advance; NotificationOutbox `hv_queued`.
699:   5. After the commit the worker is woken (S-24, auto-start).
700: - Response 201 `HvRequestResult` with Location `/qbrainai/hostile-validation/requests/{hvRequestId}`; a repeat with the same key and inputs is 200 with the stored request and its current state.
701: - Concurrency: two submissions over overlapping turns are serialized by SerializableWrite; the second sees the first's `Pending` items and is refused with `hv_turns_pending` (I-01; the unique filtered index ends a racing insert, and the retried attempt finds the winner). Two submissions over disjoint turns take consecutive cursor values, so round-robin order holds under concurrency.
702: - Errors, in order: 400 `hv_scope_invalid`, `validation_error` (submitter, key, context, `workspacePath`), `hv_scope_too_large`, `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn`, `hv_scope_empty`; 409 `conflict` (`retryable: false` key reused, `retryable: true` exhausted), `hv_turns_not_terminal`, `hv_turns_pending`, `hv_turns_already_reviewed`, `hv_no_reviewer_available` (with `details.reviewers`); 500 `evidence_corrupt` (the accepted request failed its GZIP round trip; nothing saved); 503 `audit_unavailable`.
703: 
704: ```mermaid
705: flowchart TD
706:     S(["Handler runs: POST requests"]) --> SH{"Scope, submitter, key, and context well formed?"}
707:     SH -->|"scope"| E1(["400 hv_scope_invalid, details.field"])
708:     SH -->|"submitter, key, or context"| E2(["400 validation_error, details.field"])
709:     SH -->|yes| RX[["RequirementReferenceExtractor on the context"]]
710:     RX --> SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
711:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E3(["503 audit_unavailable"])
712:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E4(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
713:     SW -->|attempt| IC[["IdempotentCreate lookup, policy Conflict"]]
714:     IC -->|"stored, same inputs"| R2(["200 the stored request"])
715:     IC -->|"key reused, other inputs"| E5(["409 conflict, retryable false"])
716:     IC -->|absent| AC[["AdmitRequestChecks"]]
717:     AC -->|refused| E6(["Refusal of AdmitRequestChecks, drawn there"])
718:     AC -->|"members and reviewer"| INS[["InsertAdmittedRequest"]]
719:     INS -->|"key collision: attempt ends"| SW
720:     INS -->|committed| R(["201 HvRequestResult; the worker is woken after the commit"])
721: ```

728:     SK -->|yes| TL[["TurnLocator: the submitting turn"]]
729:     TL -->|"InvalidIdentifier, SessionNotFound, or TurnNotFound"| E1(["400 validation_error, details.field submitter"])
730:     TL -->|found| SC
731:     SK -->|"no: Operator"| SC[["Policy HvScopeResolution"]]
732:     SC -->|refused| E2(["400 hv_scope_invalid, hv_scope_too_large, hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn, or hv_scope_empty"])

956: #### ClaimHvRunCommand: claim the next probe or review [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003, -007]
957: 
958: - Handler: `ClaimHvRunCommand(string WorkspacePath, string WorkerId) : ICommand<HvRunClaim?>`; `HvRunClaim { runId, kind, reviewerId, attempt, fenceToken, leaseExpiresUtc, hvRequestId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, probeNonce }`.
959: - Delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; then, in this order: (1) a probe: the first enabled reviewer, in pool order, with `ProbeRequestedUtc` set and fewer active runs than its `MaxConcurrentRuns`: insert its `Probe` run (`hvprobe-` key, a fresh 32-byte random `ProbeNonce` in lower-case hex), FencedLease `Claim`, clear `ProbeRequestedUtc`, and set the reviewer's `LastProbeRunId`; (2) otherwise a review: the oldest `Queued` request (by `CreatedUtc`, then `HvRequestId`) whose assignee is eligible with capacity, or whose assignee is no longer eligible and for which policy RoundRobinAssignment finds an eligible reviewer with capacity (the reassignment is recorded on the request); insert its `Review` run (`hvrun-<hvRequestId>-<nn>`, `Attempt` = `AttemptCount` + 1), FencedLease `Claim`, set the request `Running` (with `StartedUtc` on the first attempt) and `AttemptCount` + 1, and append `hv_started`. Every run records, at claim, `ClaimedUtc` and the reviewer's `ConfigurationVersion`, `ExpectedModel`, and `ExpectedEffort`. With nothing claimable it returns null and writes nothing; a request whose turns are all frozen stays `Queued` while no reviewer is eligible (ETA `Unknown`, R-18).
960: - Concurrency: the request's state, version, and the one-live-run index are checked and written in the delegate, so two workers never claim one request (W-11).

967:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E2(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
968:     SW -->|attempt| P{"An enabled reviewer with a requested probe and free capacity?"}
969:     P -->|yes| PR["Insert the Probe run with a fresh nonce; clear ProbeRequestedUtc; LastProbeRunId the new run"]

976:     NX -->|yes| Q
977:     NX -->|no| R0(["null: nothing claimable"])
978:     RR -->|"reviewer, reassignment recorded"| RV["Insert the Review run, attempt AttemptCount plus 1"]
979:     Q -->|"no Queued request"| R0

1359: ### Policy HvFinalVerification: the eight verification steps [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010, -011, -021]
1360: 
1361: Applied by FinalizeHvRequestCommand to the run's stored chunks before any transaction; each failed step returns its code, and the steps run in the diagram's order (V-1, V-8, V-2, V-3, V-4, V-5, V-6, V-7), so the log's integrity and completeness are known before any record is bound. They replace the foundation's eight receipt checks (A-05): `receipt_path` becomes V-1 (the evidence is held by the server, not found on disk), `request_meta` becomes V-3 and V-7 (the expected reviewer is recorded on the run), `verdict_block` becomes V-8, `verdict_binding` becomes V-2 and V-3, `verdict_match` becomes V-4, `reviewer_turn` becomes V-6, `reviewer_independent` becomes V-5 (amended, A-09), and `runtime_identity` becomes V-7.
1362: 
1363: - V-1 Evidence integrity (`evidence_corrupt`): the chunks run 1 to `OutputChunkCount` without a gap; each decompresses (GzipCodec), its SHA-256 equals the stored one, the chain hash equals `OutputChainSha256`, and every line parses as one JSON object (I-06).
1364: - V-2 Snapshot binding: each `hv_turn_assessment` names a member's ordinal, turn key, and admission snapshot hash (`verdict_binding_failed` otherwise), and TurnSnapshotBuilder over each turn now yields that hash (`snapshot_changed` otherwise; HvTurnFreeze makes it unreachable, and the step proves it, I-02).
1365: - V-3 Verdict binding (`verdict_binding_failed`): the `hv_verdict` record names this `hvRequestId` and run, its counts equal the members and the responses of the accepted request (the set admitted, whatever has happened to those responses since), its reviewer equals the run's reviewer, and each `hv_response_grade` names a response of the accepted request with the `ContentSha256` the accepted request recorded.
1366: - V-4 Verdict consistency (`reviewer_output_invalid`): every score is a valid lexeme (ScoreLexeme); each turn's verdict is `AGREE` exactly when ScoreVerdict derives `Pass` at the hostile thresholds and its findings hold no FAIL or UNKNOWN; the holistic verdict likewise at `max(threshold, 0.98)` (R-31); each response grade follows the foundation's `verdict_match` rule; and the overall verdict is the one predicate of R-31 over the holistic verdict, every turn's verdict, the response grades, and the findings of every scope.
1367: - V-5 Reviewer independence (`reviewer_not_independent`): the run's reviewer id differs from the request's submitter id and from its author id (S-17, S-28, P-01, P-07).
1368: - V-6 Reviewer turn (`reviewer_turn_unverified`): the `hv_reviewer_turn` record names a turn TurnLocator finds, whose agent AgentIdentity maps to the run's reviewer, whose session is neither the reviewed session nor the submitter's, created at or after the run's `ClaimedUtc`, persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), closed `completed` with class `Chore`, and whose stored result (its response, then its dialog parts in order with each part's header line removed, as foundation check 6 reads it) contains every reviewer record of the run in the order the extraction returned them (each `hv_turn_assessment`, the `hv_holistic`, each `hv_response_grade`, and the `hv_verdict`), each byte for byte in its stored normal form; a summary-only, open, or failed turn fails (P-06, R-24).
1369: - V-7 Runtime identity (`runtime_identity_mismatch`): the log holds at least one top-level `hv_provenance` line written by the worker from the CLI's runtime receipt of this run, and every one names the run's expected model (or, when the reviewer has no configured model, the model the last NONCE resolved) and expected effort (P-04).
1370: - V-8 Completeness (`reviewer_output_invalid`): exactly one `hv_verdict`, the last reviewer record; exactly one `hv_holistic`; exactly one `hv_turn_assessment` per member and one `hv_response_grade` per response of the accepted request; every FAIL and UNKNOWN finding of every scope (turn, holistic, and response) has a category, a location, evidence, and a remediation (S-13); the failures list equals every FAIL and UNKNOWN finding of every scope.

1429: ### Policy HvProbeOutcome: settle a probe run and its reviewer [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003, -009]
1430: 
1431: Applied inside the caller's transaction for a `Probe` run by CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, so a probe ends the same way whichever unit ends it, as HvRetryDecision does for a review (R-10). It is the only writer of a reviewer's readiness and probe request on behalf of a probe run. First the configuration check: a run whose `ReviewerConfigurationVersion` is not the reviewer's `ConfigurationVersion` changes nothing of the reviewer (readiness, reason, resolved model and effort, probe request, open incident), inserts no reviewer incident, and requests no probe; a stale close ends its run `Failed` with `probe_stale_configuration`, and a stale failure or expiry keeps the run outcome its caller recorded. Otherwise, by the outcome its caller hands it: a pass (from ReadinessProbeVerdict) makes the run `Succeeded` and the reviewer `Online` with `ResolvedModel` and `ResolvedEffort`, its `ReadinessReason` and `OpenIncidentId` cleared (the incident row stays), and appends `reviewer_online`; a reviewer-attributable code (FailHvRunCommand's one attribution list) makes the reviewer `Offline` with `ReadinessReason` the code and an `HvIncident` `hv-reviewer-<reviewerId>-<code>` as `OpenIncidentId`, and appends `reviewer_offline`; `evidence_corrupt` is a server fault: an `HvIncident` `hv-server-evidence_corrupt`, and the readiness unchanged; `worker_shutdown` and `lease_expired` are no outcome (the worker stopped or died), so `ProbeRequestedUtc` is set again and the same configuration is probed again, with no incident for `worker_shutdown` and the sweep's server incident for `lease_expired`. A probe that ended with a pass, a reviewer code, or `evidence_corrupt` is the settled probe of its configuration: process HvWorkerHost requests a startup NONCE only for an enabled `Unverified` reviewer whose current configuration has no settled probe (the run rows' `Kind`, `ReviewerConfigurationVersion`, `Status`, and `FailureCode` show it), so a restart never retries a settled probe, and a caller asks for a new one (S-15).

1477: ### 16.1 Process HvWorkerHost: the durable worker [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -008, -009]
1478: 
1479: A hosted `BackgroundService` per workspace application (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/Execution/HvWorkerHost.cs`), with a worker id of the host name, process id, and a random suffix. It is the only dispatcher of the internal units (R-29). At start, while `WorkerEnabled`, it requests a NONCE for every enabled `Unverified` reviewer whose current configuration has no settled probe (StartHvReviewerNonceCommand, R-10, policy HvProbeOutcome), so a probe that already settled, for example on a server fault, is not retried by a restart. Then it loops, woken by an `IChangeEventBus` wake-up or at `PollInterval`: a sweep (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, FinalizeHvRequestCommand for every `Finalizing` request it lists, FileHvIncidentCommand for every `Pending` incident), then claims until ClaimHvRunCommand returns null, starting one process RunReviewerProcess per claim. On a graceful shutdown it stops claiming and ends each of its running runs with FailHvRunCommand code `worker_shutdown`, which files no incident, marks no reviewer offline, and does not count as an attempt (policy HvRetryDecision); after a crash the leases expire instead (W-03). A 503 `audit_unavailable` from any unit stops the loop iteration and the next iteration starts from the sweep (W-12).

1500: ### 16.2 Process RunReviewerProcess: one attempt, live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008, -016]
1501: 
1502: Runs one claimed run. It builds the brief (section 13.3: the accepted request read from the `Request` evidence inside the run envelope, after AuditLedgerGuard `RecordRead` records that read, or the probe brief with its nonce, which reads no evidence); a refused read starts no process and ends the attempt without another write, so the lease expiry recovers it (W-02, W-12); a `Request` evidence that fails to decompress starts no process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision, whose attempts bound the retries, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-011-AC009). It asks the reviewer's adapter for the launch (section 16.3), starts the process with the workspace as its working directory and its plugin as a host session of its own (R-24), inside a containment bound to the worker process, so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, however abruptly (W-03; the containment, for example a process group or job object, is the adapter's, section 16.3), records the start (RecordHvRunStartCommand), and appends the `hv_brief` record as sequence 1. While the process runs it has four concurrent duties and no time limit (R-11, P-02): every line the adapter delivers goes into a buffer that is appended (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) when `OutputFlushBytes` accumulate; a flush timer appends a buffer that is not empty once `OutputFlushInterval` has passed since its first line, whether or not another line arrives, so a single line followed by silence is still appended within the interval (R-12); a heartbeat every `HeartbeatInterval` (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand) renews the lease and reads cancellation; and the process exit is awaited. `stale_fence` from any unit kills the process and ends the attempt without another write (W-03); `audit_unavailable` kills the process and ends the attempt (W-12); `evidence_corrupt` from an append (its round trip failed and nothing was saved) kills the process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision), and so does a non-retryable `conflict` from an append (a different batch under a stored sequence, or a sequence out of order), because the log's integrity can no longer be shown; a retryable `conflict` repeats the same unit call with the same sequence. Every append carries the records the adapter's extraction completed with that batch. On exit the remaining buffer is appended, the adapter's provenance lines are appended (section 16.3), and the run is closed (exit code 0, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, then FinalizeHvRequestCommand for a review whose request is `Finalizing`; a close that finds the request `CancelRequested` ends it `Canceled` instead, R-28; exit code 0 is not evidence of a review, R-11) or failed (FailHvRunCommand with `reviewer_exited_nonzero` and the exit code in its detail, or `reviewer_launch_failed` when the process never started). A cancellation read at a heartbeat kills the process and fails the run with `canceled`, which policy HvRetryDecision turns into the request's `Canceled` (R-28). Killing the process, here and in the diagrams, ends the reviewer's whole process tree, descendants included, also when the root process has already exited; and when the root exits while a descendant still holds its output pipes, the worker ends that descendant before it reads the output to its end. Without that, a descendant that outlives the reviewer would hold the run open forever, because no time limit ends a run (P-02); P14 is the same defect class in the plugin core (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011).

1564: ### 16.3 Reviewer adapter contract [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003, -008]
1565: 
1566: `IHvReviewerAdapter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Reviewers`), one implementation per reviewer id:
1567: 
1568: - `BuildLaunch(brief, reviewer)`: a `ProcessStartInfo` built as an argument list, never a shell string, with the brief on standard input or in a temporary file the adapter deletes after the run; the launch arguments come from one shared launch builder that develop's one-shot strategy also uses, so the per-CLI arguments of `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy` (`AddCodexArguments`, `AddClaudeArguments`, `AddGrokArguments`, `AddClineArguments`, `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:238-262`) are written once (DRY); processes start through the existing `IProcessSpawner` and `IProcessEnvironmentService` (`OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:18-21`), inside a containment the adapter creates at launch and binds to the worker process (for example a process group with a parent-death signal on Linux or a kill-on-close job object on Windows, settled in H1's contract step), so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, and so killing the run ends the whole tree even after the root has exited (W-03, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007-AC008, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011); develop's `DefaultProcessSpawner` starts an ordinary process and offers only an explicit kill (`src/QBrainAi.Common.AgentCli/DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16,48-51`), so H1 adds the containment. The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. Whether each reviewer's plugin can still log its turn behind its barrier (the plugin writes host-session state and calls the server) is verified in H1 (VI-03, VI-04); a reviewer that cannot fails its NONCE (R-24).
1569: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1570: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1571: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. The worker runs it as lines arrive and passes each batch's completed records to AppendHvRunOutputCommand; finalization runs it over the stored log; both get the same records (R-12). Record types the worker writes itself (`hv_brief`, `hv_provenance`, `hv_raw`) are never accepted from message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
1572: - `ReadProvenance(run)`: `hv_provenance` lines read from the CLI's own runtime receipt after the run (P-04), sources verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): for Codex, the thread's rollout `turn_context` (fields `model` and `effort`; observed `model` `gpt-6-astra`, `effort` `max`), the source the foundation's `runtime_identity` check reads (foundation section 6.3, check 8); for Claude, the session transcript under `~/.claude/projects` (the assistant message `model` and the request `effort`), written only when session persistence is on, so the launch never passes `--no-session-persistence`; for Grok, the session store `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<sessionId>/` (`summary.json` `reasoning_effort`, and a model id that `chat_history.jsonl` names `grok-4.7-build` while the events name `grok-4.7`, so H1 pins the field V-7 compares); for Copilot, the run's own JSON stream (each call's `assistant.message.model` and `user.message.responsesReasoning.effort`; `--usage-output-file` holds the model only); for Cline, none, because its run records hold the model and only whether thinking was on, so V-7 and the NONCE fail closed (L-04, D-06).
1573: - Highest effort when none is configured: the verified values of section 10 (VI-08), never develop's one-shot constants (P9).

1575: ### 16.4 Process SubmitHvFromPlugin: the plugin verb [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-005, -020]
1576: 
1577: `workflow.hv.submit` in the PowerShell core (`plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1`): process BindVerbToTurn (foundation section 4.4) binds the invocation to its turn; the verb sends SubmitHvRequestCommand through the REPL with `submitter` that turn's key and `idempotencyKey` `hv-` followed by the first 32 lower-case hex characters of the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the whole invocation identity `{ submitter: { agent, sessionId, requestId }, scope, context, contextFormat }`, so the key has 35 characters whatever the length of the ids (within the 128 of section 12), two sessions with equal request ids get different keys, and a repeat of the same call is the same request. A created or stored request is reported with its id, status, and reviewer; the watcher needs no record of it, because a terminal notification carries the submitter's turn key (R-30, section 16.5). `hv_no_reviewer_available` is reported with the context S-16 asks for: each reviewer's enabled flag, readiness, and reason from `details.reviewers`, the open incident of each `Offline` reviewer (through `workflow.hv.incidents`), and the remedy text "after the cause is fixed, NONCE the reviewer: workflow.hv.nonce <reviewerId>". Every other refusal is reported with its code, final. A retryable answer (transport outage, 503, 409 with `retryable: true`) is reported with `retryable: true` and exit 1 and is not queued in the failsafe, because the same call with the same key can simply be repeated (the reviews' no-failsafe rule, foundation section 5.2).

1592: ### 16.5 Process WatchHvNotifications: completions into the plugin [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-017, -020]
1593: 
1594: Started by process StartHostSession (foundation section 4.4) for each host session and stopped by EndHostSession; one instance per host session (`sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-watcher.pid`, the arrival bridge's pattern). It runs the REPL streaming verb `workflow.hv.watchNotifications` with `Last-Event-ID` the `lastSequence` of `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-notifications.yaml`. That one state file holds both `lastSequence` and the `inbox`, and every change to it is one atomic replace (temp file, flush, rename) under `hv-notifications.lock`. For each event the watcher writes, in that one replace, the new `lastSequence` and, when the event is `hv_completed`, `hv_failed`, or `hv_canceled` and its submitter session is this host session's MCP session (the submitter turn key the notification carries, section 12), an inbox entry keyed by the event's sequence; so a crash leaves either both or neither, and an event replayed after a crash is not added twice. Matching by the carried key needs no record of the submission, so a completion that arrives before the submit verb has returned is still inboxed. A disconnect reconnects with backoff from the recorded sequence, so nothing is missed (R-16). The prompt hook adds each undelivered inbox entry to the next prompt's context ("HV <hvRequestId> <status>, overall verdict <verdict>, sequence <n>; result: workflow.hv.result <hvRequestId>") and then marks it delivered in the same state file; a crash between the two repeats the entry at a later prompt, so delivery to the model is at least once, and the sequence makes a repeat recognizable (R-30). Plugins never call REST; the REPL holds the stream (R-30).

1599:     P -->|yes| X(["exit: one instance"])
1600:     P -->|no| C["REPL workflow.hv.watchNotifications from lastSequence"]
1601:     C --> E{"Next event?"}
1602:     E -->|"notification"| M{"Terminal kind, submitter session this host session's?"}

1604:     M -->|no| LS["Record lastSequence, one atomic replace of the state file"]

1608:     BK --> C

1623: - Storage (the subsystem keeps its entities and their single-column keys, R-25; in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/`): `HostileReviewAttemptEntity` (table `HostileReviewAttempts`, key `AttemptId` (128), with `WorkspaceId` and the root id `RequestId`, a foreign key to the request like the subsystem's execution and diagnostic rows, `HostileReviewExecutionEntity.cs:63-65`): `AttemptNumber` (int), `PoolJobId` (128), `ExecutionId` (128, null until the reviewer process starts), `Status` (16: `Claimed`, `Running`, `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Abandoned`, `Canceled`), `LeaseOwner` (256), `LeaseExpiresUtc`, `FenceToken` (long), `ClaimedUtc`, `EndedUtc`, `FailureCode` (64, sanitized), `IsDeleted`; unique filtered (`WorkspaceId`, `RequestId`) where `Status` is `Claimed` or `Running`, one live attempt per request. `HostileReviewRequestEntity` gains `AcceptedResultId` (128, set once, a key of its own, with the request's existing `Verdict` and findings as the accepted result), `AttemptCount` (int), and `IsDeleted`; its `Status` takes `Queued`, `Running`, `Completed`, and `Failed`. 1624: - Internal result types (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileReview/Execution/`): `HostileReviewAttemptClaim { attemptId, requestId, attemptNumber, poolJobId, fenceToken, leaseExpiresUtc }`; `HostileReviewRenewResult { leaseExpiresUtc }`; `HostileReviewAttemptOutcome { kind (Success, Failure, Canceled), executionId, verdict, findings, failureCode, diagnostics, counted }` (the parsed result and sanitized diagnostics only; never an artifact, a prompt, or an output line); `HostileReviewAttemptResult { status (accepted, alreadyAccepted, requeued, failed), acceptedResultId }`; `HostileReviewSweepResult { abandonedAttemptIds }`.
1625: - Identities, distinct as criterion 4 requires: the request (`RequestId`); one attempt per claim (`AttemptId`, with lease, fence, and attempt number); the AgentPool job that runs it (`PoolJobId`); one model execution per launched process (`ExecutionId`, the execution row with model, effort, agent, prompt template and version, run id, and times, criteria 1 to 3); and the one accepted terminal result (`AcceptedResultId`).
1626: - Storage boundary (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 criterion 4): the worker assembles the prompt in memory from links it reauthorizes at dispatch, reads the reviewer's output lines only to parse the result, and stores neither the prompt nor any output line nor any artifact content: only normalized identity, type, version or content hash, the parsed result, and sanitized diagnostics reach queue rows, notifications, logs, receipts, or result metadata.
1627: - Links (P3): every artifact type FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 lists resolves through its supported workspace-scoped service, the stored hash is of the resolved content (never of its id), and the limits of criterion 4 refuse more than 64 links, an artifact over 1 MiB decoded, aggregate input over 8 MiB, or uninspectable content. A link that fails its reauthorization at dispatch (missing, unauthorized, stale, or ambiguous, criteria 1, 2, and 4), or whose resolved content now exceeds a limit, launches no process: the attempt completes as a failure whose sanitized diagnostic names the link's normalized identity and the code, and no link is ever left out of a prompt silently.
1628: - Execution: bounded at-least-once across process loss (an expired lease abandons the attempt and a new one runs, up to `MaximumAttempts` counted attempts); the reviewer runs contained with its worker (W-03), and a stopped attempt ends its whole process tree (section 16.2). 1629: - Caller handling of every result: Claim null waits for the next wake-up; Renew `stale_fence` (the sweep took the attempt over) stops the reviewer and ends the attempt with no further write; Renew or Complete 503 `audit_unavailable` stops the reviewer and leaves the attempt to the lease expiry; a retryable `conflict` repeats the same call; Complete `accepted`, `alreadyAccepted`, `requeued`, `failed`, and `stale_fence` end the attempt.
1630: - Audit (P4): every unit below calls AuditLedgerGuard first, and the HostileReview entities gain `IsDeleted` in H3, so each of their writes reaches the ledger and an unwritable ledger stops the unit.
1631: - One accepted terminal result (P2): only CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand writes a result, and only while the request has none; a duplicate or late completion returns the accepted result and changes nothing, even when its fence is stale, and the sweep never changes a request that has an accepted result, replacing `AcceptReviewerOutputAsync`'s unfenced overwrite.

1719: - Delegate (SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard), in this order: a request that already has an accepted result returns `alreadyAccepted` with it and writes nothing, whatever the caller's fence; then FencedLease `Guard` (`stale_fence`: nothing changed); the attempt must be `Claimed` or `Running`; the execution row with its metadata when the outcome names one; then by outcome: a success writes the result once (`AcceptedResultId`, `Verdict`, findings), makes the attempt `Succeeded` with `EndedUtc` and the request `Completed`, and releases the lease (`accepted`); a failure makes the attempt `Failed` with its sanitized code, stores the outcome's sanitized diagnostics as the request's existing diagnostic rows (`HostileReviewDiagnosticEntity`, code and message, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/HostileReviewDiagnosticEntity.cs:23-31`), and releases the lease, and the request returns to `Queued` while counted attempts remain (`requeued`) and otherwise becomes `Failed` (`failed`); a cancellation makes the attempt `Canceled` with `worker_shutdown` (not counted) or `canceled` (counted) as the outcome says, and the request is decided as for a failure.
1720: - Results: `accepted`; `alreadyAccepted`; `requeued`; `failed`; `stale_fence`; 409 `conflict` (`retryable: true`); 503 `audit_unavailable`.

1724:     S(["CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand: attempt, fence, outcome"]) --> SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
1725:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E1(["503 audit_unavailable"])
1726:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E2(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
1727:     SW -->|attempt| AC{"Request already has an accepted result?"}
1728:     AC -->|yes| R0(["alreadyAccepted: the accepted result, nothing written"])
1729:     AC -->|no| G[["FencedLease Guard"]]
1730:     G -->|stale_fence| E3(["stale_fence: nothing changed"])

1746: - Handler: `ExpireHostileReviewLeasesCommand(string WorkspacePath) : ICommand<HostileReviewSweepResult>`; internal.
1747: - For each attempt read as `Claimed` or `Running` with an expired lease, one SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard that re-checks, in its transaction, that the attempt is still `Claimed` or `Running` and its lease still expired (otherwise skipped: it renewed or completed); the attempt becomes `Abandoned` with `EndedUtc` and its fence is incremented, so the old worker's renewal or completion is `stale_fence`; the request is then left unchanged when it has an accepted result, and otherwise returns to `Queued` while counted attempts remain and becomes `Failed` when they are spent.

1755:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E(["503 audit_unavailable: sweep ends"])

2435: ### 18.2 UC-HV-01 Manage the reviewer pool [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001]
2436: 
2437: Actors: Operator (through Director or the REPL), server. Trigger: the operator lists, inspects, enables, disables, or retunes a reviewer. Preconditions: the server started with the five reviewers configured and seeded (section 10). Main flow: the operator lists the pool (ListHvReviewersQuery), reads one reviewer (GetHvReviewerQuery), and changes its enabled flag, strategy, agent path, model, effort, or concurrency with the state version it read (UpdateHvReviewerCommand); a change to the strategy, agent path, model, or effort makes the reviewer `Unverified`, and the worker NONCEs it (UC-HV-02). Alternates: a stale state version is refused with 409 `conflict` and the operator reads again; an unknown reviewer is 404; an invalid field is 400; the audit ledger is unavailable and nothing changes (503). Postconditions: the change is stored, audited, and announced (`reviewer_unverified` when the launch changed); a disabled reviewer gets no new assignment, and the requests it held are reassigned at their next claim. Invariants: I-10; no change applies without its ledger rows.

2442:     U -. include .-> I1(("List and read reviewers"))
2443:     U -. include .-> I2(("Update with the state version (UpdateHvReviewerCommand)"))
2444:     E1(("Launch changed: Unverified, then NONCE")) -. extend .-> U
2445:     E2(("Stale state version: 409 conflict")) -. extend .-> U
2446:     E3(("Audit ledger unavailable: 503")) -. extend .-> U
2447: ```

2449: ### 18.3 UC-HV-02 NONCE a reviewer [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003]
2450: 
2451: Actors: operator or any agent, HV worker, reviewer agent. Trigger: a reviewer is `Unverified` (startup or a launch change, requested by the worker) or `Offline` after its cause was fixed (requested by a caller, S-15). Preconditions: the reviewer is enabled. Main flow: the caller requests a NONCE (StartHvReviewerNonceCommand); the worker claims the probe (ClaimHvRunCommand), launches the reviewer with a probe brief carrying a fresh nonce (RunReviewerProcess), streams its output (AppendHvRunOutputCommand), appends the adapter's provenance, and closes the run (CloseHvRunOutputCommand); policy ReadinessProbeVerdict passes: the nonce is echoed, the provenance shows the expected model and effort, and the reviewer logged its own turn; the reviewer becomes `Online` with its resolved model and effort. Alternates: a probe already requested or running is reported without a second probe; a disabled reviewer is refused with 409 `hv_reviewer_disabled`; the probe fails (wrong nonce, wrong or missing provenance, no reviewer turn, launch failure, nonzero exit) and the reviewer stays or becomes `Offline` with an incident filed through triage (UC-HV-09); the probe's stored log fails its integrity check, a server fault, and a server incident is filed while the reviewer's readiness is unchanged; the reviewer is reconfigured while the probe runs, and the old probe, whether it closes, fails, ends with a shutdown, or loses its lease, changes nothing of the reviewer while the newer probe request waits (HvProbeOutcome); the worker dies during a probe of the current configuration and the sweep requests it again; the worker restarts after a probe settled on a server fault and requests no new probe until a caller asks. Postconditions: the reviewer's readiness reflects a probe of this moment (S-27); `reviewer_online` or `reviewer_offline` is announced. Invariants: only a passing NONCE moves a reviewer to `Online` (R-10).

2456:     WK(["HV worker"]) --- U
2457:     RV(["Reviewer agent"]) --- U
2458:     U -. include .-> I1(("Probe run with a fresh nonce (RunReviewerProcess)"))
2459:     U -. include .-> I2(("Decide (ReadinessProbeVerdict)"))
2460:     E1(("Already requested or running: no second probe")) -. extend .-> U
2461:     E2(("Disabled reviewer: 409")) -. extend .-> U
2462:     E3(("Probe failed: Offline, incident filed")) -. extend .-> U
2463:     E4(("Worker died: probe requested again")) -. extend .-> U
2464:     E5(("Stored log corrupt: server incident, readiness unchanged")) -. extend .-> U
2465:     E6(("Reconfigured while probing: stale probe, readiness unchanged")) -. extend .-> U
2466:     E7(("Restart after a settled probe: no automatic retry")) -. extend .-> U

2469: ### 18.4 UC-HV-03 Submit an HV request [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-002, -004, -005, -006, -013, -018]
2470: 
2471: Actors: model (through its plugin) or operator (through Director), any client, server. Trigger: a caller wants a turn, an inclusive range of turns, or a whole session reviewed (S-03, S-11). Preconditions: the turns to review are terminal; for an agent caller, its own turn is bound by the plugin (BindVerbToTurn). ## Action

Load the global operator profile, then turn it into an active Claude operating model for the rest of the session. This is not a summary task. It is a context-recovery and trust-calibration task.

The profile is GLOBAL. It lives in `~/.claude/profile/` and applies in every session and every repo. It does not depend on the active project's `memory/` directory.

## Read Contract

1. Read this `SKILL.md` in full before acting.
2. Read every markdown file in `~/.claude/profile/` in full, excluding skill-port files named `add-profile*.md`. Since 2026-10-13 the profile is the single file `PROFILE-MERGED.md`; the 20 earlier profile files are archived under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T151859/` and are not read. 3. Do not rely only on a hardcoded list. If new profile files exist, read them too.
4. Read files in full, not snippets. Never skip a read because a prior tool result claims the content is already loaded or unchanged.
5. Treat the read as read-only. Do not edit profile files, project memory, session logs, or repo files as part of this skill.

## Claude Synthesis Contract

After reading, build an internal operator model with these layers:

1. Hard constraints: commands, tools, source control, formatting, storage interfaces, approval boundaries, serialization rules, HV request/response jsonl receipts, entire HV results in the MCP session log, and the 98 percent HV accuracy/completeness approval threshold.
2. Trust contract: accuracy first, bring receipts, distinguish observation from inference, concede mistakes quickly, and verify from authoritative artifacts.
3. Execution style: decision-complete plans when changes are ambiguous or high blast radius; direct execution when the user gives an explicit implementation command.
4. Frustration detectors: if the user has already narrowed the symptom, make that symptom the primary requirement. Do not keep pursuing broader abstractions after acknowledging the narrower instruction.
5. Session deltas: integrate corrections and failures from the current conversation, especially recent trust breaks. Use them to adjust behavior immediately.
6. Inference layer: infer what the profile implies about how the user experiences the current interaction. Label those inferences as inferences, not facts.

## Required Behavior After Load

For future turns in the same session:

1. Bring receipts for the exact claim being made, not adjacent claims.
2. Prefer source-pinned facts over memory, stale markers, or convenient assumptions.
3. When corrected, stop and restate the exact correction before continuing.
4. If a diagnostic clue is precise, test that clue directly before broad exploration.
5. When asked what was learned, include both facts and useful inferences. Do not give a generic preference summary.
6. When asked about frustration or trust, connect the profile to the actual session behavior. Name the contract violation and the consequence.
7. Keep private profile content out of the response unless the user explicitly asks for it.
8. Do not restate the full profile by default.

## Response Contract

Default confirmation after load:

`<timestamp> - Profile loaded: read <N> global profile files.`

After reading the profile, state how the information learned will shape your behavior in the context of the current session. Do this on every load, not only when asked. Tie the statement to the live session (current task, recent corrections, and in-flight work), not a generic preference recap.

If the user asks what you learned, answer with:

1. Observed facts from the profile.
2. Inferences from those facts.
3. Current-session implications.
4. Receipts: file paths and counts read.

If the user asks whether you understand frustration, answer with:

1. Observation: what happened.
2. Inference: why that violated the user's operating contract.
3. Consequence: what behavior must change now.
4. Receipts: exact files read and any command output or artifact that supports the claim.

## 5. Development process: Byrd Development Process v4 (BDPv4)

BDPv4 applies to every plan for project implementation work, no exceptions. Operator statement of 2026-10-13 (verbatim): "BDPv4 says TDD Tests must cover 100% of AC and must be implemented and tested with mock data to prove the test is correct before any code is written for the implementation."

- Requirements drive tests: every acceptance criterion is covered by TDD tests (100 percent of ACs).
- Every test is implemented and run against mock data to prove the test itself is correct before any implementation code is written.
- Only then is implementation code written, and the implementation is done when the full applicable suite is green (section 4.5).
- The plan decides everything about its shape: how it is cut into phases or slices, where its gates and hostile validations fall, and when its pull requests are created and merged (resolutions of 2026-10-13: "HV cadence is an artifact of the plan, not a standing rule." and "The plan decides everything"). No standing phase or pull-request sequence applies outside the plan.
- BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to code and documentation in the scope of implementing the project. User-directed operational actions are not BDPv4 work (section 7.2).

### 5.1 BDPv4 TDD procedure in detail (explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)

Verbatim from MEMORY-PROCEDURE-002: "Byrd Development Process v4 TDD procedure, explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08. Applies globally to all agents, repositories, and implementation increments. This records the required BDPv4 procedure. Previous red-before-green descriptions were incorrect and were never a valid description of this process."

1. Requirements drive tests. Start from the approved functional requirements, use cases, technical requirements, TEST requirements, and acceptance criteria. Map each test to the behavior it proves. For parity ports, preserve the original test's inputs, assertions, boundary cases, errors, and side-effect checks; a matching test count alone does not establish parity.
2. Write the tests and their independent mocks or scripted fakes before writing or changing the production implementation for that increment. Supply deterministic contract-derived fixtures and expected responses through the intended dependency boundary. Expected values must come from requirements or independently pinned original behavior, never from the implementation under test. A mock must exercise the test's actual assertions and relevant interactions; merely returning true or bypassing the asserted path is not validation.
3. Prove that the tests discriminate correct and incorrect behavior. Run correct mock responses through every required assertion. Deliberately supply wrong mock responses, boundary values, omissions, exceptions, or interactions to prove that the corresponding assertions reject them. Capture these rejection checks as expected negative controls inside a passing test harness. These controls are evidence that the assertions work, not an acceptable failing unit suite or permission to begin production code with red tests.
4. Establish a documented green mock gate BEFORE production implementation: all required tests pass against the correct mocks, every planned negative control is rejected as expected, and there are no unexplained failures, skips, or unexecuted required cases. Fix deficient tests or mocks and repeat this gate before proceeding. Do not substitute NotImplementedException stubs, deliberately red production tests, or a claim of 'red observed' for this evidence.
5. Only after the mock gate is green, implement or correct the real production behavior. Bind the SAME test cases, inputs, assertions, expected results, and interaction checks to the real implementation through the approved seam. Change the provider or adapter as needed, but do not weaken assertions, replace expected results with production output, silently remove cases, or count mock-only success as proof of real behavior.
6. Run the production-bound tests and fix the implementation until they pass. Refactor only while maintaining green tests. Run the full applicable suite, required build checks, and integration or runtime checks before advancing the phase gate. Any reduced scope, deferred cases, or baseline exception requires explicit operator agreement and must be stated with its denominator.
7. Retain chronological receipts proving the order: requirement/test IDs, test and fixture paths or hashes, exact mock-run commands and outputs, passing counts, negative-control results, production edits, real-run commands and outputs, and full applicable suite results. Distinguish mock evidence, real implementation evidence, and live runtime evidence. Keep durable MCP session actions and design decisions current.
8. Apply independent hostile review at the required acceptance gates unless the operator explicitly waives or postpones it. Record a temporary waiver and the complete catch-up review backlog. Never fabricate review acceptance or mark unfinished goals, TODOs, requirements, acceptance criteria, or plan steps done. A pause stops development and auxiliary work until explicitly resumed; a request to persist this procedure authorizes only that memory work.

Also stated (MEMORY-DEVPROCESS-003, verbatim): "RED tests are not acceptable. BDPv4 requires mocking data to prove tests work to green before starting code." The April 2026 BDPv4 essay (MEMORY-DEVPROCESS-001 and -004) still describes a Red, Green, Refactor cycle; where it differs, the operator statement above and this procedure govern. The essay is kept in the project extract.

### 6.1 PowerShell only

- Every script, script tool, and automation step is PowerShell (`pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive`), and so is every script or tool a plan designs. Operator, verbatim: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell.", "This should have already been the standard for plugins.", and "I have not chosen PowerShell for scripting because of Microsoft or Windows. I have chosen it because it is simply the best tool for the job." Never frame PowerShell as a platform preference; it is chosen on merit (object pipeline, native serialization, one language on Linux and Windows).
- Before designing, check the design against the standards that already exist. Drift from an existing standard is your failure, not a new requirement.
- Build JSON and YAML payloads from native objects and serialize them; never handwrite them as string literals.
- Every script is checked before it runs against data (operator, verbatim: "Run your script through PS Analyzer before running it against data."): PowerShell parser errors plus Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer at Warning and Error, all fixed or justified (a suppression carries a written justification), state-changing scripts dry-run with -WhatIf first, and the analyzer result is reported with the run.
- Always combine elevated actions into a single script.

### 6.2 Bash (resolution of 2026-10-13)

Bash has two uses only: installing PowerShell, and launching `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File <script.ps1>` with literal arguments. No `-Command`, no inline code, no dollar signs or backticks, no pipes, `&&`, or `cd` in the Bash string (operator, verbatim, 2026-10-13: "You should be avoiding bash"). Searching, reading, git inspection, and checks run inside PowerShell scripts; every piece of logic, one-off checks included, lives in a `.ps1` written with an editor tool and analyzed first, never through Bash heredocs or redirects. Never write files from Bash (no `cat >`, heredocs, `sed ... >`, `tee`, `rm`). The Write/Edit tools are not a shell.
